Maps each known city to its canonical region ({@code Sydney -> NSW}, 24 * {@code Melbourne -> VIC}, {@code Brisbane -> QLD}); any other city resolves 25 * to {@link #UNKNOWN}. 26 */ 27 public final class CityRegion { 28 29 /** The region returned for a city that is not in the table. */ 30 public static final String UNKNOWN = "UNKNOWN"; 31 32 private static final Map CITY_REGION = Map.of( 33 "Sydney", "NSW", 34 "Melbourne", "VIC", 35 "Brisbane", "QLD"); 36 37 private CityRegion() { 38 } 39 40 /** 41 * Return the canonical region for the given city, or {@link #UNKNOWN} when 42 * the city is not in the table. 43 * 44 * @param city the city to look up (may be {@code null}) 45 * @return the canonical region string, or {@code "UNKNOWN"} 46 */ 47 public static String regionFor(String city) { 48 return CITY_REGION.getOrDefault(city, UNKNOWN); 49 } 50 } 51

The ranges are keyed by the region derived from the city via 28 * {@link CityRegion}: {@code NSW 2000-2099}, {@code VIC 3000-3099} and 29 * {@code QLD 4000-4099} (all inclusive). A city whose region has no known range 30 * (including {@link CityRegion#UNKNOWN}) accepts any postcode. Format (four 31 * digits) is enforced separately by Bean Validation on the request DTO, so this 32 * class only checks membership of the region's range. 33 */ 34 public final class PostcodeValidator { 35 36 /** Region -> inclusive 4-digit postcode range {@code {low, high}}. */ 37 private static final Map REGION_POSTCODES = Map.of( 38 "NSW", new int[] {2000, 2099}, 39 "VIC", new int[] {3000, 3099}, 40 "QLD", new int[] {4000, 4099}); 41 42 private PostcodeValidator() { 43 } 44 45 /** 46 * Returns whether the given postcode is acceptable for the given city. 47 * 48 *

An absent postcode is always acceptable (the field is optional), and a 49 * city whose region has no known range accepts any postcode. Otherwise the 50 * postcode must fall within its region's inclusive range. 51 * 52 * @param city the owner's city 53 * @param postcode the submitted postcode, may be {@code null} or blank 54 * @return {@code true} when the postcode is acceptable for the city 55 */ 56 public static boolean isValidForCity(String city, String postcode) { 57 if (postcode == null || postcode.isBlank()) { 58 return true; 59 } 60 int[] range = REGION_POSTCODES.get(CityRegion.regionFor(city)); 61 if (range == null) { 62 return true; 63 } 64 int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode.trim()); 65 return value >= range[0] && value <= range[1]; 66 } 67 } 68

## Summary

The locality derivation now prefers the postcode, falling back to the city table only when the postcode is absent or in no known range. I kept the code well-factored with one responsibility per unit:

- **`model/PostcodeRegion.java`** (new) — single source of truth for the region↔postcode-range table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). Exposes `regionFor(postcode)` (region whose disjoint range contains the postcode, else `null`) and `hasRange(region)`.
- **`model/Locality.java`** (new) — composes the precedence rule: `PostcodeRegion.regionFor(postcode)` first, then `CityRegion.regionFor(city)` as fallback.
- **`model/Owner.java`** — `getLocality()` now delegates to `Locality.of(city, postcode)` instead of the city-only lookup.
- **`model/CityRegion.java`** — unchanged; still owns the city-to-region fallback table.
- **`rest/validation/PostcodeValidator.java`** — refactored to reuse `PostcodeRegion` instead of carrying a duplicate range table. Since ranges are disjoint, a postcode is valid for a city's region exactly when its own postcode-derived region matches, preserving the original validation behavior.

Known cities still resolve to the same region (e.g. Sydney@2000 → NSW), while a VIC-range postcode on an unlisted city now correctly disambiguates to VIC — matching the new acceptance test `functionalityPostcodePreferredOverCity`.
